Blocks Palestinian Islamic Jihad members from entering the United States
Blocks people who took part in the October 7, 2023 attacks on Israel from entering the United States
Blocks all Palestinian Liberation Organization members from entering the United States
Stops October 7 attackers from seeking asylum
Stops October 7 attackers from getting protection from deportation

118-hr-676.one_liner: Require NOAA to work with local communities on ocean acidification problems
provisions: NOAA must work with state, local, and tribal groups on ocean acidification problems
NOAA must help these groups improve their programs for dealing with acidification
NOAA must help groups share their successful work as examples for other communities
A federal advisory board on ocean acidification must include two tribal representatives

supporters: Supporters say this would help coastal communities fight ocean acidification by requiring NOAA to work directly with state, local, and tribal groups on their programs.
Supporters say adding two tribal representatives to the federal advisory board ensures Native American voices are heard on ocean acidification decisions.
Supporters say this would help communities learn from each other by requiring NOAA to share successful acidification programs as examples.
critics: Critics say this creates new federal mandates requiring NOAA to collaborate with state, local and tribal groups without providing additional funding.
Critics say requiring NOAA to assist groups in improving their programs and share information could create administrative burden and duplicate existing work.

118-hr-6918.one_liner: Block a rule change for pregnancy centers that get welfare program money
provisions: Stops the government from applying a new funding rule to pregnancy centers
Lets pregnancy centers keep getting money from a program that helps poor families
Covers centers that offer pregnancy counseling, testing, diapers, baby clothes, and family support
The blocked rule would make states prove the money is used reasonably for program goals

118-hr-6976.one_liner: Make drunk driving a reason to deport or block non-citizens from entering
provisions: Stops non-citizens from entering the US if convicted of drunk driving
Stops non-citizens from entering the US if they admit to drunk driving
Lets the government deport non-citizens convicted of drunk driving

118-hr-734.one_liner: Ban people born male from competing in women's and girls' sports at federally funded schools
provisions: Stops people born male from competing in women's and girls' sports at schools that get federal money
Says this rule applies under Title IX, the law that stops sex discrimination in schools
Defines sex by a person's biology at birth
Lets people born male practice with women's teams if it does not take away spots from women

118-hr-7217.one_liner: Fund military aid to Israel and US operations after attacks in Israel
provisions: Provides emergency military funding for the year starting October 2023
Pays to replace weapons and equipment the US gave to Israel
Covers costs of current US military operations in the Middle East region
Funds Israel's Iron Dome and other missile defense systems
Increases security funding for US embassies affected by the Israel attacks
Pays for emergency evacuations of US government workers and citizens
Lets the President transfer more military equipment to Israel

118-hr-7024.one_liner: Expand tax credits for families and increase business tax breaks
provisions: Increases tax credits for families with children
Lets businesses write off equipment costs faster to reduce their taxes
Sets different tax rules for Taiwan residents who earn US income
Increases tax breaks for people who lost money in disasters and wildfires
Increases tax credits for building affordable housing

118-hr-7463.one_liner: Keep the government running through March 2024 and change student aid rules
provisions: Funds federal agencies through March 8, 2024 for some and March 22, 2024 for others to prevent government shutdown
Sets a floor of negative $1,500 for student income when calculating financial aid in 2024-2025
Sets a floor of $0 for student income when calculating financial aid starting in 2025-2026
Provides additional funding for Federal Pell Grants starting in 2025

118-hr-753.one_liner: Require VA hospitals to install on-site medical waste treatment systems
provisions: Requires VA hospitals to install systems that treat medical waste on-site instead of shipping it elsewhere
VA must create a cost analysis to figure out which hospitals would save money with these systems
Only hospitals that would save money get the new waste treatment systems

supporters: Supporters say installing on-site medical waste treatment systems at VA hospitals would save money by ending the need to ship waste to outside facilities.
Supporters say the required cost analysis model ensures taxpayer money is only spent at hospitals that would actually save money.
critics: Critics say the upfront costs to install and operate medical waste treatment systems at VA facilities could be expensive for taxpayers.
Critics say operating medical waste treatment systems on-site at VA hospitals could create safety risks for staff and patients.

118-hr-815.one_liner: Remove the 24-month care requirement for new veterans' emergency treatment reimbursement
provisions: Removes the rule that veterans must have received VA care within 24 months before getting emergency treatment to qualify for reimbursement
Lets veterans get VA reimbursement for emergency treatment at non-VA hospitals if the treatment happens within 60 days of enrolling in VA healthcare
Covers emergency treatment costs for newly enrolled veterans who have not yet used VA services

supporters: Supporters say this helps veterans who just signed up for VA care get emergency treatment paid for at non-VA hospitals within 60 days.
Supporters say removing the 24-month rule means new VA patients can get emergency care covered without waiting two years.
critics: Critics say covering emergency treatment for newly enrolled veterans will cost the VA more money by paying for additional non-VA hospital bills.
Critics say this may cause more veterans to go to non-VA emergency rooms instead of VA hospitals.

118-hr-788.one_liner: Stop the federal government from sending settlement money to outside groups
provisions: Stops the government from making legal settlements that send money to outside groups
Allows payments to repair damage caused by the defendant or pay for services
Lets officials be fired or lose money if they break this rule
Requires agencies to report their settlements for 7 years
Requires government watchdogs to report on rule violations

supporters: Supporters say this stops settlement money from going to outside groups that were not harmed, ensuring taxpayer funds return to the Treasury instead.
Supporters say the 7-year reporting rule will show the public how agencies spend settlement dollars and which groups receive payments.
Supporters say officials who break these rules can be fired or lose money, creating real consequences for violations.
critics: Critics say the narrow exceptions for 'actual harm' and 'services' could block settlement funds from going to community programs that help areas affected by corporate wrongdoing.
Critics say the 7-year reporting requirement will create extra paperwork and costs for agencies that must track and report all settlement details.
Critics say this rule could make companies less willing to settle cases if they cannot direct money to environmental cleanup or community restoration projects.

118-hr-813.one_liner: Require a government study of how well America attracts foreign business investment
provisions: Requires the Department of Commerce and Government Accountability Office to study foreign investment in America
The study examines how well America attracts businesses from trusted countries to invest here
Agencies must review current government policies that affect foreign investment
The study includes recommendations for bringing more foreign businesses to America

118-hr-7888.one_liner: Extend FBI surveillance powers for 5 years with new rules
provisions: Lets the FBI keep using a surveillance program for 5 more years to spy on people outside America
Requires FBI supervisors to approve searches about Americans caught in this surveillance
Makes the FBI Deputy Director approve any searches about elected officials or government workers
Bans political appointees from approving searches about politicians
Creates punishments for FBI agents who break surveillance rules including firing for intentional misconduct
Increases criminal penalties for people who violate surveillance laws
Requires sworn statements for surveillance requests and limits using information from political groups or news sources

supporters: Supporters say this bill adds important oversight by requiring FBI supervisors to approve searches about Americans caught in surveillance.
Supporters say the ban on political appointees approving searches about elected officials prevents partisan misuse of surveillance powers.
Supporters say the penalties including firing for intentional misconduct will stop FBI agents from breaking surveillance rules.
critics: Critics say this extends mass surveillance of people outside America for 5 more years without ending warrantless searches of Americans' data.
Critics say FBI supervisors can still approve searches about Americans without a warrant, which violates privacy rights.
Critics say the exception allowing searches to prevent threats to life or serious harm is too broad and could be misused.

118-hres-104.one_liner: Condemn China for flying a spy balloon over the United States
provisions: Condemns China for violating US territory with a spy balloon
Says China lied about what the balloon was for
States US policy should stop foreign spy aircraft from entering US territory

supporters: Supporters say this resolution makes it official US policy to stop foreign spy aircraft from violating US territory.
Supporters say this condemns China for sending the spy balloon over US airspace without permission.
Supporters say this calls out China for lying about the balloon's true purpose as a surveillance tool.
critics: Critics say this resolution only makes statements but creates no new laws to actually stop spy balloons.
Critics say condemning China could make diplomatic relations worse without fixing the surveillance problem.
Critics say existing US policy already prevents foreign aircraft from entering US territory without permission.

118-hres-11.one_liner: Create a House committee to study competition with China
provisions: Creates a committee in the House of Representatives
Committee has up to 16 members chosen by House leaders
Committee studies how China competes with the US in business, technology, and security
Committee writes recommendations for Congress about competing with China

supporters: Supporters say the 16-member committee will investigate China's economic, technological, and security progress to help the US compete.
Supporters say the committee will write policy recommendations for Congress about competing with China.
critics: Critics say the 16-member committee costs money for staff and operations that could be used elsewhere.
Critics say creating a committee focused on China competition could harm diplomatic relations with China.

118-hres-12.one_liner: Create a House subcommittee to investigate federal agencies' information gathering on citizens
provisions: Creates a House subcommittee with up to 13 members to investigate federal agencies
The subcommittee investigates how executive branch agencies collect information on U.S. citizens
Looks for activities that are illegal, unconstitutional, or unethical
Must report findings by January 2, 2025
The subcommittee ends 30 days after filing its report

supporters: Supporters say the 13-member subcommittee will protect citizens from illegal government spying by investigating how executive agencies collect information on Americans.
Supporters say requiring a final report by January 2, 2025 ensures Congress gets answers about unconstitutional surveillance activities within a clear deadline.
critics: Critics say creating another subcommittee wastes taxpayer money on partisan investigations instead of focusing on real legislative priorities.
Critics say the subcommittee interferes with legitimate law enforcement work by second-guessing how agencies investigate threats to national security.

118-hres-114.one_liner: Remove Representative George Santos from the House of Representatives
provisions: Removes George Santos from his seat in Congress
Stops him from voting in the House
Ends his pay and benefits from Congress
Leaves an empty House seat that needs to be filled

supporters: Supporters say this would remove Santos from his seat in Congress and stop him from voting on laws
Supporters say this would end Santos's pay and benefits from Congress paid by taxpayers
Supporters say this would open the House seat so voters can elect a new representative
critics: Critics say this would remove an elected representative before his term ends
Critics say this would leave the House seat empty until a special election is held
Critics say this removes Santos without letting voters decide in the next regular election

118-hres-166.one_liner: Allow votes on requiring inflation estimates and canceling retirement investment rules
provisions: Allows a House vote on requiring inflation estimates for Executive orders that cost money
Allows a House vote on canceling rules about how retirement plans invest money
Sets time limits for debate on both issues

118-hres-132.one_liner: Express condolences for earthquake victims in Turkey and Syria
provisions: Expresses sadness for people who died in earthquakes in Turkey and Syria on February 6, 2023
Thanks aid workers and rescue teams helping earthquake victims
Criticizes Syria's government for using the disaster to avoid international pressure

118-hres-240.one_liner: Condemn Russia for forcing down a US military drone
provisions: Officially condemns Russia for forcing down a US military drone
States the drone was operating in international airspace when forced down
Declares Russia's attempts to recover the drone threaten US national security

supporters: Supporters say this resolution sends a clear message that Russia violated international law by forcing down a US drone in international airspace.
Supporters say condemning Russia's attempts to recover the drone protects US national security interests.
Supporters say this official condemnation shows America will not tolerate attacks on US military equipment operating legally in international waters.
critics: Critics say this resolution could make tensions with Russia worse without solving the drone problem.
Critics say formal condemnations like this might lead Russia to take more aggressive actions against US military operations.
Critics say this resolution is just words that do not actually stop Russia from threatening US national security.

118-hres-241.one_liner: Set rules for the House to consider a bill about parental rights in schools
provisions: Sets the rules for how the House will debate H.R. 5 about parental rights in public schools
Allows the House to vote on H.R. 5 under specific time limits and procedures

supporters: Supporters say parents have the right to know what curriculum their children are taught in public schools and should be notified about lesson plans.
Supporters say this bill would give parents access to school library books and materials so they can stay involved in their child's education.
Supporters say parents should be told when schools discuss topics about gender identity or sexuality with their children.
critics: Critics say these rules could let parents remove books from school libraries and limit what teachers can teach in classrooms.
Critics say the bill could harm LGBTQ+ students by forcing schools to tell parents private information about their children's conversations with counselors.
Critics say this could create conflicts between parents and teachers over science lessons and social studies topics.

118-hres-298.one_liner: Set House debate rules for Title IX sports and DC police bills
provisions: Allows the House to consider a bill about Title IX sports requirements
Allows the House to consider disapproving DC's police reform law
Sets the debate time and voting procedures for both bills

supporters: Supporters say this rule allows Congress to require schools to use biological sex at birth for Title IX sports teams.
Supporters say the rule lets Congress block DC's police reform law that changes how officers work.
Supporters say the debate rules give both sides time to discuss these issues.
critics: Critics say using biological sex at birth would ban transgender students from sports teams matching their identity.
Critics say blocking DC's police reform ignores what local voters wanted in 2022.
Critics say the debate time limits prevent full discussion of these complex issues.

118-hres-199.one_liner: Set up House votes on federal employee speech restrictions, water regulations, and COVID information release
provisions: Allows the House to vote on a bill that stops federal employees from pushing for censorship while working
Allows the House to vote on canceling EPA water regulations that expand which areas count as federal waters
Allows the House to vote on requiring intelligence agencies to release secret information about how COVID started

supporters: Supporters say H.R. 140 would protect free speech by stopping federal employees from pushing tech companies to remove legal content while on the job.
Supporters say H.J. Res. 27 would stop the EPA from claiming control over more private land through expanded water rules that hurt farmers and property owners.
Supporters say S. 619 would give the public the right to know how COVID started by forcing intelligence agencies to release hidden information about the virus origins.
critics: Critics say H.R. 140 would make it harder for federal agencies to work with social media companies to stop dangerous misinformation about health and elections.
Critics say H.J. Res. 27 would weaken clean water protections by allowing more pollution in streams and wetlands that flow into drinking water sources.
Critics say S. 619 could put national security at risk by forcing the release of secret information that reveals how intelligence agencies gather information and protect sources.

118-hres-260.one_liner: Allow a vote on increasing American oil and gas production
provisions: Sets rules to allow a vote on an energy bill
The energy bill would increase American oil and gas production
The energy bill would speed up permits for oil wells and pipelines
The energy bill would increase exports of American oil and gas
The energy bill would make it easier to mine minerals needed for batteries

supporters: Supporters say this rule allows a vote on a bill that would increase American oil and gas production, reducing energy costs for families.
Supporters say the rule enables consideration of legislation that speeds up permits for oil wells and pipelines, creating thousands of jobs.
Supporters say this allows a vote on a bill that makes it easier to mine minerals needed for batteries, helping America compete with China.
critics: Critics say this rule enables a bill that increases oil and gas production, worsening air pollution in communities near drilling sites.
Critics say the rule allows consideration of legislation that speeds up permits without proper environmental review of oil wells and pipelines.
Critics say this enables a bill that prioritizes oil and gas exports over keeping energy affordable for American families.

118-hres-363.one_liner: Express support for National Police Week and honor officers killed while working
provisions: Expresses support for recognizing National Police Week
Honors law enforcement officers across the United States
States that officers need equipment, training, and resources to stay safe while working
Honors law enforcement officers for acts of sacrifice and heroism
Expresses sympathy to families of officers killed while working

supporters: Supporters say this resolution honors law enforcement officers across the United States who died protecting people.
Supporters say recognizing National Police Week helps families of fallen officers know their sacrifice is remembered.
Supporters say stating that officers need equipment, training, and resources shows Congress knows police work is dangerous.
critics: Critics say this resolution talks about officers needing equipment and training but gives them no actual money for these things.
Critics say this resolution honors law enforcement officers but takes no action to actually improve police safety.

118-hres-311.one_liner: Encourage more countries to sign peace agreements with Israel
provisions: Encourages the US and Israel to work together more closely on economic and security matters
Urges other countries to normalize relations with Israel like the UAE, Bahrain, Morocco, and Sudan have done
Calls for peace agreements to deliver real economic and security benefits to people in those countries

supporters: Supporters say expanding the Abraham Accords beyond UAE, Bahrain, Morocco, and Sudan would bring economic and security benefits to more people in the region.
Supporters say stronger US-Israel cooperation on economic and security matters would help create stable relationships between Israel and Arab nations.
Supporters say the focus on delivering real benefits to citizens would ensure peace agreements help ordinary people.
critics: Critics say the resolution adds more countries without checking if the current four Abraham Accords members are getting promised benefits.
Critics say encouraging more nations to normalize relations with Israel while ignoring Palestinian concerns could hurt peace efforts.
Critics say the emphasis on US-Israel cooperation benefits those two countries more than Arab nations being asked to normalize relations.

118-hres-377.one_liner: Call for Russia to release detained American citizens and residents
provisions: Calls on Russia to release Evan Gershkovich, an American news reporter detained since March 2023
Tells all US government officials to bring up Gershkovich's case when talking with Russia
Calls for Russia to release Paul Whelan
Shows support for all American citizens and residents detained in Russia and other countries
Shows sympathy for the families of detained Americans

supporters: Supporters say this puts pressure on Russia by requiring all US government officials to bring up Gershkovich's case in every meeting with Russian officials.
Supporters say this shows Congress backs four specific Americans detained in Russia: Gershkovich, Whelan, Fogel, and Kara-Murza.
Supporters say this gives comfort to families of detained Americans by showing the US government will not forget them.
critics: Critics say this resolution has no legal power to force Russia to release any of the four detained Americans.
Critics say requiring all US officials to raise these cases in every meeting with Russia could hurt other important diplomatic talks.
Critics say making these detention cases more public could lead Russia to treat Gershkovich, Whelan, and other detained Americans worse.

118-hres-382.one_liner: Recognize Jewish American Heritage Month and call for leaders to fight antisemitism
provisions: Recognizes Jewish American Heritage Month as time to celebrate Jewish Americans
Calls on elected officials to condemn antisemitism
Calls on faith leaders to fight antisemitism
Calls on community leaders to fight antisemitism

supporters: Supporters say recognizing Jewish American Heritage Month celebrates the specific contributions of Jewish Americans to American society and culture.
Supporters say calling on elected officials, faith leaders, and community leaders to condemn antisemitism helps fight rising antisemitic incidents.
critics: Critics say the call on faith leaders to fight antisemitism interferes with religious freedom and separation of church and state.
Critics say the call for elected officials to condemn antisemitism creates government interference in speech issues.

118-hres-327.one_liner: Set debate rules for a debt ceiling bill and a trade duties resolution
provisions: Sets the rules for how the House will debate a bill about raising the debt ceiling
Sets the rules for how the House will debate a resolution to cancel a Commerce Department rule about trade duties

supporters: Supporters say this rule allows the House to vote on the debt ceiling increase bill and the resolution about Commerce Department trade duties.
Supporters say this follows standard House procedures for bringing these measures to the floor for debate and voting.
critics: Critics say this rule limits debate time for the debt ceiling increase and prevents members from offering amendments.
Critics say this rule rushes consideration of the Commerce Department trade duties resolution without full discussion.

118-hres-398.one_liner: Allow House votes on three bills related to law enforcement
provisions: Lets the House vote on a bill that makes attacking a police officer a reason to deport non-citizens
Lets the House vote on a bill that allows federal law enforcement officers to buy their retired service weapons
Lets the House vote on a resolution supporting local police and opposing efforts to defund police departments

supporters: Supporters say making assault of law enforcement officers a deportable offense would protect police and remove non-citizens who attack officers from the country.
Supporters say allowing federal law enforcement officers to buy their retired service weapons helps officers keep familiar firearms for personal protection after they leave service.
Supporters say the resolution backing local police and opposing defunding efforts sends a strong message of support to law enforcement agencies across the country.
critics: Critics say the deportation provision for assaulting officers could separate immigrant families and lacks protections for due process rights.
Critics say allowing federal officers to purchase retired weapons could put more firearms into circulation without proper tracking.
Critics say the resolution opposing police defunding efforts blocks needed reforms and ignores community calls for police accountability.

118-hres-383.one_liner: Set rules for House votes on border security and unemployment fraud recovery bills
provisions: Allows the House to debate and vote on a border security bill
Allows the House to debate and vote on a bill about recovering stolen unemployment money
Sets the time limits and rules for discussing both bills

supporters: Supporters say this rule allows the House to consider border security legislation in an orderly manner
Supporters say this rule provides floor time for legislation to recover fraudulently obtained unemployment payments
critics: Critics say this rule limits the time available to debate border security measures
Critics say this rule restricts opportunities to offer amendments to the unemployment fraud legislation

118-hres-461.one_liner: Condemn using school buildings to house non-citizens who are not admitted to the US
provisions: Condemns using elementary school buildings to house non-citizens
Condemns using high school buildings to house non-citizens
Applies to schools that currently serve students
Targets non-citizens who are not admitted to the United States
Creates a formal congressional statement of disapproval

supporters: Supporters say elementary and secondary school facilities should be used for students' education, not to house non-citizens who are not admitted to the United States.
Supporters say using school buildings that serve children for shelter takes away resources and space from students.
critics: Critics say this resolution only creates a formal statement of disapproval without solving housing problems for non-citizens.
Critics say condemning the use of elementary and secondary school facilities could prevent communities from providing emergency shelter during humanitarian crises.

118-hres-456.one_liner: Set up rules for Congress to vote on raising the debt ceiling
provisions: Sets up the rules for the House to vote on H.R. 3746 about raising the debt ceiling
Decides how long members can debate the debt ceiling bill
Sets rules for what changes members can make to the bill
Moves the debt ceiling bill toward a final House vote

supporters: Supporters say this rule allows the House to have an organized debate on raising the debt ceiling to avoid a government default.
Supporters say the rule gives members time to discuss the debt ceiling increase while moving toward a needed vote.
Supporters say structured rules help the House consider important bills like H.R. 3746 in an orderly way.
critics: Critics say the rule limits how long members can debate such an important issue as raising the debt ceiling.
Critics say the rule restricts what changes members can make to the debt ceiling bill.
Critics say the rule rushes consideration of H.R. 3746 without allowing enough time for full review.

118-hres-429.one_liner: Set House voting rules for bills on fentanyl, truck pollution, and student loans
provisions: Sets voting rules for a bill that would change how fentanyl-like drugs are regulated
Schedules a vote to cancel EPA pollution standards for heavy trucks
Plans a vote to block Education Department rules on student loan changes

supporters: Supporters say this rule allows Congress to quickly vote on making fentanyl-like substances illegal under federal drug laws.
Supporters say this gives Congress a chance to stop EPA pollution rules that would cost trucking companies money and hurt the economy.
Supporters say this lets Congress review Education Department changes to student loan rules before they affect borrowers.
critics: Critics say this blocks EPA standards that would cut pollution from heavy trucks and improve air quality.
Critics say this stops Education Department rules that would help people with student loan problems get relief.
Critics say bundling these three different issues together makes it harder for Congress members to vote on each one separately.

118-hres-495.one_liner: Set up House votes on five bills that block federal regulations
provisions: Allows a House vote to cancel an ATF rule about pistol braces on firearms
Allows a House vote to require Congress approval before major federal agency rules take effect
Allows a House vote to change how courts review agency rule interpretations
Allows a House vote to block federal money from being used to ban gas stoves
Allows a House vote to stop the Energy Department from setting energy rules for cooking appliances

supporters: Supporters say this rule allows Congress to vote to overturn the ATF rule that would reclassify pistol braces as short-barreled rifles, protecting gun owners from new restrictions.

Supporters say this rule allows Congress to vote to require approval before major federal agency rules take effect, giving elected officials more control over regulations that affect millions of Americans.
Supporters say this rule allows Congress to vote to block federal money from being used to ban gas stoves and to stop the Energy Department from setting new energy standards for cooking appliances.
critics: Critics say this rule could allow Congress to block ATF firearms regulations and Energy Department appliance standards without expert review.
Critics say this rule could delay agency rules that protect public safety by requiring Congressional approval before major regulations take effect.
Critics say blocking the Energy Department's cooking appliance standards could cost consumers money on energy bills and slow progress on energy efficiency.

118-hres-463.one_liner: Allow House votes on 4 bills limiting federal agency power
provisions: Allows voting on a bill requiring Congress to approve major federal rules before they take effect
Allows voting on a bill changing how courts review agency decisions about laws and regulations
Allows voting on a bill stopping federal money from being used to ban gas stoves
Allows voting on a bill blocking Energy Department rules on cooking appliance efficiency standards

supporters: Supporters say this rule allows voting on H.R. 277 which would give Congress oversight over major federal regulations before they take effect.

Supporters say this rule allows voting on H.R. 1615 and H.R. 1640 which would protect consumer choice by prohibiting federal funds to ban gas stoves and blocking Energy Department cooking appliance efficiency standards.
Supporters say this rule allows voting on H.R. 288 which would give courts more authority to review agency interpretations of laws and regulations.
critics: Critics say this rule fast-tracks consideration of H.R. 277 which would slow down federal safety and environmental regulations by requiring Congressional approval.
Critics say this rule allows voting on bills that would prevent federal agencies from regulating gas stove emissions and cooking appliance energy efficiency standards.
Critics say this rule enables consideration of H.R. 288 which would weaken agency expertise in interpreting complex regulations.

118-hres-492.one_liner: Criticize Iran for attacking Baha'i religious minority and call for penalties on officials
provisions: Says Iran attacks Baha'i religious minority and breaks international agreements
Asks Iran to free Baha'is jailed for their religion
Tells Iran to stop spreading hate against Baha'is
Asks Iran to end policies that treat religious minorities unfairly
Asks President to put penalties on Iranian officials who abuse human rights

supporters: Supporters say this resolution would protect Iran's 300,000 Baha'i religious minority from state-sponsored persecution and imprisonment.
Supporters say calling for sanctions on Iranian officials who abuse human rights would create real consequences for persecution of Baha'is.
Supporters say urging Iran to release Baha'is jailed solely for their religion would free innocent people from prison.
critics: Critics say condemning Iran's government could hurt diplomatic efforts to improve relations with Iran.
Critics say this non-binding resolution won't actually force Iran to stop persecuting Baha'is or change its policies.
Critics say pushing for sanctions on Iranian officials could escalate tensions and make Iran less likely to cooperate on other issues.

118-hres-5.one_liner: Adopt new House rules for the 118th Congress
provisions: Lets any House member call a vote to remove the Speaker
Blocks bills that increase government spending without cuts elsewhere
Ends automatic debt ceiling suspension when Congress passes a budget
Requires 3 out of 5 House members to approve tax rate increases
Lets Congress cut federal workers' pay or specific programs through spending bills
Removes union rights for some congressional staff
Requires bill sponsors to state the single topic their bill covers

supporters: Supporters say allowing any single House member to call a vote to remove the Speaker increases accountability by giving individual representatives more power over leadership.
Supporters say requiring spending cuts to offset new mandatory spending and requiring 3 out of 5 House members to approve tax increases will help control government spending and protect taxpayers.
Supporters say the Holman rule lets Congress cut specific programs or federal worker salaries through spending bills, giving lawmakers more oversight of government operations.
critics: Critics say letting one House member trigger a Speaker removal vote could create constant chaos and prevent Congress from governing effectively.
Critics say blocking bills that increase spending without cuts elsewhere could prevent emergency aid or funding for programs that help families and communities.
Critics say removing collective bargaining rights from congressional employees and allowing salary cuts through the Holman rule unfairly targets federal workers.

118-hres-489.one_liner: Censure Representative Adam Schiff for misleading conduct
provisions: Formally censures Representative Adam Schiff
Condemns Adam Schiff for conduct that misleads the American people
Orders the Ethics Committee to investigate his conduct

supporters: Supporters say the formal censure sends a clear message that misleading the American people has consequences.
Supporters say the Ethics Committee investigation is needed to examine Schiff's conduct for potential rule violations.
critics: Critics say the censure resolution is politically motivated rather than based on documented misconduct.
Critics say the Ethics Committee investigation wastes time and resources without clear evidence of violations.

118-hres-529.one_liner: Send impeachment resolution against President Biden to House committees
provisions: Sends an impeachment resolution against President Biden to the Committee on Homeland Security
Sends the same resolution to the Committee on the Judiciary
The impeachment resolution involves President Biden's actions on immigration and the southern border

supporters: Supporters say this resolution would allow the Committee on Homeland Security and Committee on the Judiciary to properly investigate President Biden's immigration policies at the southern border.
Supporters say referring H. Res. 503 to committees follows the right constitutional process for examining impeachment charges.
critics: Critics say sending the impeachment resolution to two committees wastes Congress's time on political attacks instead of fixing immigration problems.
Critics say this referral process diverts the Committee on Homeland Security and Committee on the Judiciary from their regular work.

118-hres-521.one_liner: Formally condemn Representative Adam Schiff for misleading conduct
provisions: Formally condemns Representative Adam Schiff for conduct that misleads the American people
Orders the Ethics Committee to investigate Schiff's conduct

supporters: Supporters say the formal condemnation of Representative Schiff is needed to hold him accountable for making misleading statements to the American people.
Supporters say ordering the Ethics Committee to investigate Schiff's conduct will help Congress maintain proper standards for its members.
critics: Critics say formally condemning Representative Schiff without listing specific wrongdoing makes this censure politically motivated rather than fact-based.
Critics say directing the Ethics Committee to investigate Schiff's conduct wastes time on partisan attacks instead of real ethics violations.

118-hres-583.one_liner: Let the House vote on the 2024 defense budget
provisions: Allows the House to continue working on the 2024 military budget bill
Lets the House debate and vote on defense spending and troop numbers

supporters: Supporters say this rule allows the House to continue working on H.R. 2670, the 2024 defense bill that sets military spending and troop numbers.
Supporters say this rule lets Congress debate and vote on funding for Department of Defense programs and military construction.
critics: Critics say this rule limits debate time on H.R. 2670, the National Defense Authorization Act for 2024.
Critics say this rule restricts amendment opportunities for the defense budget bill that affects military personnel and programs.

118-hres-582.one_liner: Set the rule for Congress to debate and vote on the fiscal year 2024 defense bill
provisions: Allows Congress to consider a bill that would fund the military for fiscal year 2024
Sets the process for debating defense spending and troop levels
Enables voting on military construction and energy programs

supporters: Supporters say this rule allows Congress to vote on funding for military activities and personnel for fiscal year 2024
Supporters say this process enables lawmakers to set troop strength levels needed for the armed forces
Supporters say this rule permits voting on military construction projects and Department of Energy defense programs
critics: Critics say this rule limits debate time on defense spending and military personnel strength decisions
Critics say this process rushes consideration of military construction and energy program funding
Critics say this rule restricts the ability to offer amendments to defense spending priorities

118-hres-524.one_liner: Set up House votes on mortgage fees, health insurance, and school shelters
provisions: Allows the House to vote on canceling recent mortgage pricing changes by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac
Allows the House to vote on a bill about health reimbursement arrangements for individual health insurance
Allows the House to vote on condemning the use of schools to shelter people not admitted to the United States

supporters: Supporters say this allows the House to vote on canceling recent up-front loan level pricing adjustments by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac for single-family mortgages.
Supporters say this enables consideration of health reimbursement arrangements integrated with individual health insurance coverage.
Supporters say this allows the House to vote on condemning the use of elementary and secondary school facilities to shelter people not admitted to the United States.
critics: Critics say this rule combines three unrelated policy areas - mortgage pricing, health insurance, and school facilities - in one procedural vote.
Critics say this allows votes on resolutions about elementary and secondary school facility use without separate consideration.
Critics say this enables consideration of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac pricing changes alongside unrelated health insurance and school measures.

118-hres-712.one_liner: Set up House votes on defense spending, natural gas exports, and gun rights resolution
provisions: Allows the House to vote on funding the Defense Department for the year ending September 2024
Allows the House to vote on removing limits on natural gas exports and imports
Allows the House to vote on a statement against New Mexico's Governor for gun policies

supporters: Supporters say this rule allows Congress to vote on Defense Department funding for fiscal year 2024 that troops need.
Supporters say this rule lets Congress vote on removing limits on natural gas exports that hurt American energy companies.
Supporters say this rule allows Congress to condemn New Mexico's governor for gun policies that violate Second Amendment rights.
critics: Critics say this rule rushes Defense Department spending through Congress without enough time to review the budget.
Critics say this rule forces a vote on removing natural gas export limits that protect the environment from pollution.
Critics say this rule wastes Congress time on a political statement against New Mexico's governor instead of solving real problems.

118-hres-681.one_liner: Set up a House vote on preventing elimination of internal combustion engine sales
provisions: Creates rules for the House to debate a bill about internal combustion engines
Allows a vote on whether to prevent elimination of gas and diesel engine sales

supporters: Supporters say this rule allows the House to vote on preventing the elimination of gas and diesel engine sales.
Supporters say this creates proper debate rules for lawmakers to discuss protecting internal combustion engines.
critics: Critics say this rule advances a bill that would block efforts to limit car pollution under the Clean Air Act.
Critics say this procedural step helps protect gas engine sales over air quality rules.

118-hres-614.one_liner: Set up House votes on military funding and canceling two wildlife rules
provisions: Sets up a House vote on funding for military construction and veteran programs for the year ending September 2024
Sets up a House vote on canceling protection rules for lesser prairie chickens
Sets up a House vote on canceling protection rules for northern long-eared bats

supporters: Supporters say this allows Congress to vote on military construction and veteran funding for the year ending September 2024
Supporters say this lets elected officials review Fish and Wildlife Service rules protecting lesser prairie chickens that may limit farming and oil drilling
Supporters say this gives Congress a chance to review bat protection rules that may affect how landowners use their property
critics: Critics say this could delay important funding for veteran programs and military construction projects in 2024
Critics say this threatens federal protections for lesser prairie chickens that scientists say are declining in number
Critics say this could remove protections for northern long-eared bats that are already struggling to survive

118-hres-680.one_liner: Set rules for the House to debate two bills
provisions: Sets rules for how the House will debate a bill about car engine sales and clean air laws
Sets rules for how the House will debate a bill that pays for the military in 2024

supporters: Supporters say this rule allows the House to consider both the car engine sales bill and the 2024 military funding bill in an organized way.
Supporters say the rule ensures Congress can act quickly on defense spending that funds the military through September 2024.
Supporters say structured debate rules help lawmakers focus on the key issues in both bills.
critics: Critics say the rule limits how long lawmakers can debate the car engine and military funding bills.
Critics say the rule restricts opportunities for members to offer changes to either the car engine or defense spending bills.
Critics say rushing consideration of both bills prevents proper review of military spending and clean air rules.

118-hres-597.one_liner: Set rules for Congress to consider bills about aviation and school shelters
provisions: Lets Congress vote on a bill to renew FAA funding and extend aviation programs
Lets Congress vote on a bill to stop schools from sheltering non-citizens

supporters: Supporters say the FAA reauthorization would extend funding for aviation safety programs that protect millions of air travelers each year.
Supporters say continuing FAA programs maintains the air traffic control systems that prevent plane crashes and delays.
Supporters say the school shelter restriction would protect classroom resources and school buildings for American students who need them for education.
critics: Critics say the FAA reauthorization spends taxpayer money on federal programs without requiring specific safety improvements or cost reductions.
Critics say the school shelter ban would prevent local communities from helping vulnerable families and children who need temporary housing during emergencies.
Critics say blocking schools from providing shelter could leave asylum seekers and other non-citizens without safe places to stay.

118-hres-75.one_liner: Allow House votes on bills to end COVID emergency rules and vaccine mandates
provisions: Allows a vote on ending the national emergency declared in March 2020 for COVID
Allows a vote on requiring government agencies to study telework during COVID and plan future remote work
Allows a vote on ending the public health emergency for COVID
Allows a vote on stopping vaccine requirements for healthcare workers in federal programs

supporters: Supporters say this allows Congress to vote on ending the national emergency powers that have been in place since March 2020.
Supporters say this would require federal agencies to study their telework practices during COVID and create plans for future remote work.
Supporters say this lets lawmakers vote to eliminate vaccine requirements for healthcare workers in Medicare, Medicaid, and other federal health programs.
critics: Critics say ending the national emergency could remove federal tools needed to respond to future health threats.
Critics say requiring agencies to study telework during COVID could burden them with administrative work.
Critics say removing vaccine mandates for healthcare workers could put vulnerable patients in federal health programs at risk.

118-hres-730.one_liner: Set debate rules for three government spending bills
provisions: Sets time limits and rules for changing the military spending bill for 2024
Sets time limits and rules for changing the homeland security spending bill for 2024
Sets time limits and rules for changing the extra government spending bill for 2024

supporters: Supporters say this rule provides clear time limits for debate on the defense spending bill (H.R. 4365) and homeland security spending bill (H.R. 4367) for 2024.
Supporters say the structured rules for changing the three appropriations bills help Congress act on government funding before the fiscal year ends.
critics: Critics say the time limits for changing the military spending bill (H.R. 4365) restrict lawmakers' ability to offer amendments to defense spending.
Critics say limiting the rules for changing the homeland security spending bill (H.R. 4367) reduces Congress's ability to modify funding decisions.

118-hres-76.one_liner: Remove Representative Ilhan Omar from the House Foreign Affairs Committee
provisions: Removes Representative Ilhan Omar from the House Committee on Foreign Affairs

supporters: Supporters say removing Representative Omar from the Foreign Affairs Committee would improve oversight of U.S. foreign policy.
Supporters say this action would address concerns about committee member statements on international issues.
Supporters say the committee would function more effectively without Representative Omar as a member.
critics: Critics say removing Representative Omar from the Foreign Affairs Committee strips an elected member of Congress from an important role.
Critics say this resolution unfairly targets one specific representative for removal from committee work.
Critics say taking Representative Omar off the Foreign Affairs Committee reduces Minnesota voters' voice on foreign policy issues.

118-hres-723.one_liner: Set debate rules for four government spending bills in Congress
provisions: Allows Congress to debate how much money to give the Defense Department for the year starting October 2023
Allows Congress to debate how much money to give Homeland Security for the year starting October 2023
Allows Congress to debate how much money to give the State Department and foreign aid programs for the year starting October 2023
Allows Congress to debate how much money to give Agriculture Department and FDA for the year starting October 2023

supporters: Supporters say this rule lets Congress debate funding for the Defense Department, Homeland Security, State Department, and Agriculture Department for the year starting October 2023.
Supporters say without this rule, these four agencies could run out of money and have to shut down important programs.
Supporters say the rule follows the normal process for Congress to review how much taxpayer money each department gets.
critics: Critics say this rule rushes votes on spending bills for defense, border security, foreign aid, and farm programs without enough time to study them.
Critics say combining four different department budgets makes it hard for lawmakers to ask detailed questions about each agency's spending.
Critics say the rule moves too fast and doesn't give Congress enough time to check how billions in taxpayer money will be used.

118-hres-83.one_liner: Set up House votes on socialism statement and removing committee member
provisions: Allows the House to debate and vote on a statement against socialism
Allows the House to debate and vote on removing a member from a committee

supporters: Supporters say this rule allows the House to debate and vote on H. Con. Res. 9 to make a statement about socialist economic policies and their effects on American businesses and workers.
Supporters say this rule allows the House to debate and vote on H. Res. 76 to remove a specific member from a House standing committee.
critics: Critics say this rule uses House debate time for H. Con. Res. 9, a non-binding resolution, instead of bills that provide funding or change laws.
Critics say this rule allows debate on H. Res. 76 to target one member for committee removal without following established House disciplinary procedures.

118-hres-863.one_liner: Impeach the Secretary of Homeland Security for border security and fentanyl issues
provisions: Impeaches Alejandro Mayorkas as Secretary of Homeland Security
Charges him with high crimes and misdemeanors
Cites his handling of border security issues
Cites his handling of fentanyl problems

supporters: Supporters say Mayorkas failed to secure the border, allowing record numbers of people to cross illegally during his time as Secretary of Homeland Security.
Supporters say his poor handling of the fentanyl crisis has cost American lives as deadly drugs keep flowing across the border.
Supporters say these failures in border security and fentanyl prevention are serious enough to count as high crimes and misdemeanors.
critics: Critics say policy disagreements about border security do not meet the legal standard of high crimes and misdemeanors required for impeachment.
Critics say Mayorkas was following existing laws and administration policies, making impeachment wrong for policy disputes.
Critics say this impeachment effort targets political differences rather than actual criminal conduct by the Secretary.

118-hres-966.one_liner: Condemn rape and sexual violence by Hamas and call for accountability
provisions: Condemns rape and sexual violence used as weapons of war by Hamas since October 7, 2023
Calls on all countries to make rape and sexual assault illegal
Calls for holding all perpetrators of sexual violence accountable

supporters: Supporters say this condemns rape and sexual violence used as weapons of war by Hamas since October 7, 2023.
Supporters say this calls for holding all perpetrators of sexual violence accountable, including state and non-state armed groups.
Supporters say this calls on all countries to make rape and sexual assault illegal.
critics: Critics say this resolution creates no new laws or enforcement mechanisms to prevent sexual violence.
Critics say this focuses only on Hamas actions since October 7, 2023, while not addressing sexual violence in other conflicts.
Critics say this provides no funding or resources to help victims of sexual violence.

118-hres-90.one_liner: Demand that China release American citizen Mark Swidan
provisions: Demands that China release Mark Swidan immediately
Condemns China for blocking Swidan from meeting with U.S. diplomats
Condemns China for denying Swidan medical care
Mark Swidan is an American citizen sentenced to death in China for drug charges

supporters: Supporters say this would help Mark Swidan, a US citizen sentenced to death in China, who a UN working group found is being held arbitrarily and in violation of human rights.
Supporters say China is denying Swidan access to US diplomats and medical care, which breaks basic protections that American citizens should get when arrested abroad.
Supporters say the UN working group on arbitrary detention determined that Swidan's case violates the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
critics: Critics say this resolution interferes with China's court system by demanding they overturn Swidan's drug conviction and death sentence.
Critics say pressuring China to release a prisoner convicted of drug charges could harm diplomatic relations between the US and China.
Critics say this sets a bad precedent for Congress to demand foreign governments reverse their court decisions in criminal cases.

118-hres-947.one_liner: Allow Congress to vote on three bills about settlements, labor rules, and car chargers
provisions: Sets up votes on three bills in the House of Representatives
Allows a vote on a bill limiting donations made through government lawsuit settlements
Allows a vote on canceling a labor rule about when two companies both count as an employer for the same worker
Allows a vote on canceling a rule that lets the government buy foreign-made electric vehicle chargers instead of American-made ones

supporters: Supporters say limiting settlement donations would stop the government from directing taxpayer money from lawsuit settlements to third-party groups that were not harmed by the original violation.

Supporters say canceling the joint employer rule would protect franchise owners and contractors from being held responsible for labor violations by companies they work with but do not directly control.
Supporters say requiring American-made electric vehicle chargers would create manufacturing jobs in the United States instead of sending contracts to foreign companies.
critics: Critics say blocking settlement donations would prevent the government from directing money to communities and organizations harmed by corporate violations, reducing compensation for victims.
Critics say keeping the current joint employer rule helps workers hold both staffing agencies and the companies that use their services accountable when labor laws are broken.
Critics say requiring only American-made EV chargers could slow down building the charging network needed for electric cars if domestic companies cannot meet demand quickly enough.

118-hres-957.one_liner: Condemn the administration's border policies and urge the President to change them
provisions: Formally condemns the current administration's border policies
Urges the President to end current border policies

supporters: Supporters say this resolution would formally condemn border policies they believe create national security and public safety risks along the southwest border.
Supporters say this resolution would urge the President to end current border policies that allow too many people to cross illegally.
critics: Critics say this resolution would only condemn and urge action but would not change any actual border policies or enforcement.
Critics say this resolution wrongly calls current policies 'open borders' when border enforcement and deportations continue under the administration.

118-hres-994.one_liner: Allow House votes on expanding tax deductions and denouncing energy policies
provisions: Allows the House to vote on a bill that would change tax deduction limits for married couples
Allows the House to vote on a resolution criticizing the Biden administration's energy policies

supporters: Supporters say this would help married couples in high-tax states who currently face a $10,000 limit on state and local tax deductions.
Supporters say Biden's energy policies like restricting oil drilling have increased gas prices for working families.
Supporters say federal regulations on fossil fuel companies cost jobs in traditional energy industries.
critics: Critics say changing the SALT deduction limit would mainly help wealthy households in expensive states rather than middle-class families.
Critics say this energy resolution is just political messaging that will not lower gas prices or create jobs.
Critics say Biden's climate policies reduce pollution and create new jobs in clean energy manufacturing.

118-hres-980.one_liner: Allow House votes on four bills about crime and immigration
provisions: Sets the rules for House debates on four bills
Allows a vote on new penalties for running from federal police
Allows a vote on removing non-citizens who commit Social Security fraud
Allows a vote on removing non-citizens who helped attack Israel
Allows a vote on removing non-citizens with drunk driving records

supporters: Supporters say the new penalties for fleeing federal officers would protect law enforcement and the public from dangerous high-speed chases.
Supporters say removing non-citizens who commit Social Security fraud would protect taxpayer money and prevent identity theft that costs billions annually.
Supporters say deporting non-citizens with drunk driving convictions would remove dangerous drivers who put families at risk on roads.
critics: Critics say these deportation rules would separate families when parents with minor drunk driving offenses are removed from their citizen children.
Critics say the Social Security fraud provision could deport people for paperwork errors or using fake documents just to work and support families.
Critics say the fleeing federal officers penalty creates double punishment by adding immigration consequences on top of criminal charges.

118-hres-969.one_liner: Allow House votes on bills about pregnant students, pregnancy centers, and border policies
provisions: Sets up a House vote on requiring colleges to share information about rights and resources for pregnant students
Sets up a House vote on stopping the Health Department from restricting funding for pregnancy centers
Sets up a House vote on a resolution criticizing Biden administration border policies

supporters: Supporters say requiring colleges to share information about rights and resources would help pregnant students know about available support and accommodations.
Supporters say stopping the Health Department from restricting pregnancy center funding would protect organizations that provide services to pregnant women.
Supporters say the resolution criticizing Biden border policies would address security concerns along the southwest border.
critics: Critics say requiring colleges to disseminate pregnancy information creates new federal mandates on higher education institutions.
Critics say protecting pregnancy center funding would limit the Health Department's ability to ensure organizations provide comprehensive reproductive health services.
Critics say the border resolution is political messaging that does not provide specific solutions to immigration issues.

118-hres-996.one_liner: Set up House votes on impeaching the Homeland Security Secretary and changing healthcare coverage decisions
provisions: Sets up a House vote on impeaching Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas
Sets up a House vote on stopping federal health programs from weighing treatment costs against patient benefits

supporters: Supporters say this rule allows Congress to vote on holding Secretary Mayorkas accountable for border security failures under his leadership.
Supporters say this rule lets Congress vote to protect disabled and elderly patients from cost-based care rationing in Medicare and Medicaid.
critics: Critics say the impeachment vote wastes time that should be spent on border security funding and immigration reform.
Critics say blocking cost-effectiveness measures in federal health programs could increase Medicare and Medicaid spending without improving care quality.

118-hres-97.one_liner: Allow House votes to end COVID vaccine travel rules and overturn two DC laws
provisions: Sets up a vote to end the rule requiring foreign travelers to show proof of COVID-19 vaccination
Sets up a vote to overturn a DC law that lets non-citizens vote in local elections
Sets up a vote to overturn DC's new criminal code that reduces penalties for some crimes

supporters: Supporters say ending the vaccination requirement for foreign travelers would boost tourism and remove barriers for international visitors.
Supporters say overturning DC's law would ensure only U.S. citizens can vote in local elections, as intended by the Constitution.
Supporters say blocking DC's new criminal code would keep tougher penalties for crimes like carjacking and robbery to protect public safety.
critics: Critics say removing vaccination requirements for foreign travelers could increase the spread of COVID-19 and other diseases.
Critics say overturning DC's voting law takes away the city's right to decide who can participate in local elections about schools and neighborhood issues.
Critics say blocking DC's criminal code reform ignores years of work by local officials to reduce prison sentences and focus on rehabilitation.

118-s-316.one_liner: Cancel military authorizations for using force against Iraq
provisions: Cancels the laws that let the President use military force against Iraq
Removes Congress's approval for military action in Iraq
Ends the legal authority for ongoing military operations in Iraq

supporters: Supporters say this bill removes outdated laws that let the President use military force against Iraq without getting new approval from Congress.
Supporters say ending the legal authority for ongoing military operations in Iraq will prevent old war powers from being used for new conflicts.
critics: Critics say removing Congress's approval for military action in Iraq could limit the President's ability to protect American troops and interests in the region.
Critics say canceling the laws that let the President use military force against Iraq could make it harder to fight terrorist groups that operate there.

118-s-2226.one_liner: Fund the military and set troop levels for the year starting October 2023
provisions: Gives money to the Department of Defense to buy weapons, ships, and military equipment
Sets how many troops can serve in active duty and reserves
Pays for construction projects on military bases
Sets rules for military pay and benefits
Funds research on military technology
Gives money to Department of Energy programs that maintain nuclear weapons

supporters: Supporters say this bill sets active duty and reserve troop levels to maintain military readiness.
Supporters say this bill authorizes construction of military family housing and base facilities for service members.
Supporters say this bill funds procurement of aircraft, ships, missiles and military equipment.
critics: Critics say this bill establishes a new Civilian Cybersecurity Reserve that adds federal positions.
Critics say this bill authorizes Department of Energy nuclear weapons spending through the National Nuclear Security Administration.
Critics say this bill authorizes new military construction projects across multiple service branches.

118-s-2073.one_liner: Make federal agencies list outdated reports in their budget requests
provisions: Federal agencies must list outdated reports in their yearly budget requests
Agencies must say whether each old report should be ended, changed, or made less frequent
Agencies must show which laws require each report
Agencies must list which congressional committees get each report

supporters: Supporters say requiring agencies to list outdated reports in their budget requests will help cut government waste.
Supporters say making agencies recommend whether to end or change each old report will save taxpayer money on unnecessary paperwork.
Supporters say showing which laws require each report will help Congress see what reports they actually need.
critics: Critics say requiring agencies to review all their reports and make recommendations will create more work and cost more money.
Critics say letting agencies decide whether reports should be ended could eliminate important oversight that protects the public.
Critics say making agencies list which congressional committees get reports puts bureaucrats in charge of deciding what Congress needs to know.

118-s-112.one_liner: Expand lifelong benefits for children of Vietnam veterans with spina bifida
provisions: Gives lifelong health care, job training, and money to children of Vietnam veterans who have spina bifida
Covers children with birth defects whose mothers served in Vietnam
Creates care teams at the Department of Veterans Affairs to check on these children every 180 days
Sets up an advisory council to improve care for covered children
Requires different parts of Veterans Affairs to work together to help these children

supporters: Supporters say this bill helps children with spina bifida get health care, job training, and money for their entire lives because their birth defects were caused by their parents' service in Vietnam.
Supporters say the care teams that check on these children every 180 days will make sure no child is forgotten or loses needed medical care.
Supporters say children of women Vietnam veterans with birth defects also deserve lifelong help because their mothers served their country.
critics: Critics say providing lifelong health care, job training, and monthly payments to children with spina bifida will cost taxpayers millions of dollars each year.
Critics say creating new advisory councils and care teams at the Department of Veterans Affairs will add more government workers and increase spending.
Critics say expanding coverage beyond spina bifida to include other birth defects of women Vietnam veterans makes the program too broad and expensive.

118-s-111.one_liner: Require federal agencies to post plain-language summaries of proposed rules
provisions: Requires federal agencies to include a website link to a summary when they propose new rules
Summaries must be 100 words or less and written in plain language
Summaries must be posted on regulations.gov

supporters: Supporters say the 100-word limit and plain language requirement would help regular citizens understand complex federal rules that affect their daily lives.
Supporters say requiring summaries on regulations.gov would make it easier for people to find and read about new government rules before they take effect.
Supporters say forcing agencies to write simple summaries would make the government more open about what new rules actually do.
critics: Critics say requiring agencies to write summaries for every proposed rule would create extra work and slow down important rulemaking.
Critics say the 100-word limit might force agencies to leave out key details that people need to understand how rules affect them.
Critics say the cost of creating and posting these summaries would waste taxpayer money on paperwork instead of enforcement.

118-s-3250.one_liner: Let victims of the 1988 Pan Am Flight 103 bombing watch court cases remotely
provisions: Lets victims of the 1988 Pan Am Flight 103 bombing watch criminal court cases from home
Applies to the case against Abu Agila Mohammed Mas'ud Kheir Al-Marimi
